question: Can interpolation theory be expressed as a trainable graph architecture that unifies regression, PDE solution, and inverse calibration while retaining numerical-method structure?

key_findings.claim: An interpolating neural network assigns each mesh node a compact-supported interpolation function and trains nodal values and optionally coordinates; one-hop linear interpolation recovers linear FEM while wider message passing recovers richer generalized-FEM-like bases.
key_findings.evidence: The construction discretizes the input domain, builds interpolation-valued message passing with the Kronecker-delta property, and contracts the resulting basis functions with nodal values.

key_findings.claim: On the authors' deterministic 10-input/5-output regression benchmark, similarly sized INNs reached the training-MSE threshold in substantially fewer epochs than MLPs.
key_findings.evidence: A 2,250-parameter INN reached MSE 4e-4 at epoch 34 versus epoch 217 for a 2,285-parameter MLP; the comparison fixes optimizer, learning rate, and batch size but reports a training threshold rather than a broad generalization study.

key_findings.claim: The PDE examples recover interpolation-order convergence behavior and the additive-manufacturing studies report large storage and runtime reductions, but several headline system comparisons include estimated baselines.
key_findings.evidence: The Poisson experiment compares H1-error convergence of PINN and interpolation bases; the space-time-parameter heat model and online-control studies report sub-10-micrometer resolution and 18--31x training speedups, while Figure 3 marks some FDM/FEM points as estimated.

method.core_idea: Turn classical interpolation bases into graph message-passing functions whose nodal coefficients and geometry can be optimized by machine-learning losses.
method.mechanism: Discretize an input domain, construct compact-supported shape functions by local message passing, contract them with nodal values, and optionally apply CP or Tucker tensor decomposition on regular grids to reduce high-dimensional parameter growth.
assumptions: The target mapping is sufficiently smooth and local for the selected interpolation family and mesh.
A regular-grid tensor decomposition has useful low rank when used to avoid exponential dimensionality.
The reported FEM-like convergence arguments transfer only to the specified interpolation and PDE settings.

techniques.role: Represents local numerical basis functions as graph-node hidden states.
Optimizes nodal values and optionally coordinates for data, PDE, or calibration losses.
Factorizes regular-grid coefficients to reduce parameter and storage cost.

evaluations.setting: Synthetic 10-input/5-output regression, 1D Poisson PDE, and additive-manufacturing surrogate, calibration, and heat-transfer problems.
evaluations.metric: Training MSE threshold and epochs, H1 error versus degrees of freedom, trainable parameters, storage, and wall-clock time.
evaluations.result: INN variants converge faster or use fewer parameters in the selected studies and exhibit expected interpolation convergence slopes; the AM study reports high-resolution simulation on one GPU.
evaluations.baseline: MLPs, PINNs, FEM, single-scale FDM, and variational multiscale FEM, with some large AM baseline points estimated rather than executed.

limitations: The benchmarks are a small, heterogeneous set and do not establish performance across operator-learning datasets or geometries.
Some headline compute comparisons use estimated competitor points, complicating reproducible speedup claims.
Regular-grid tensor compression depends on favorable low-rank structure and may fail on discontinuities or highly irregular domains.
Training-loss convergence is not a substitute for out-of-distribution accuracy or calibrated uncertainty.
failure_modes: Local interpolation can overfit sparse data or miss globally coupled, nonsmooth structure.
A required CP/Tucker rank can grow rapidly and erase the claimed dimensionality advantage.
Moving nodes may yield poor meshes or unstable optimization without geometric constraints.
reusable_insights: Embedding known numerical bases into trainable architectures can preserve interpretable approximation properties.
Parameter-count claims should separate basis coefficients, mesh degrees of freedom, and decomposition ranks.
Engineering speedups need measured end-to-end baselines at matched accuracy.
open_questions: How does INN compare with DeepONet and FNO on standard operator-learning suites at matched error and compute?
What rank and mesh-adaptivity diagnostics predict when compression will fail?
Can posterior or ensemble uncertainty guide adaptive node placement and safe online control?

competitive_landscape.title: Physics Informed Deep Learning (Part I): Data-driven Solutions of Nonlinear Partial Differential Equations
competitive_landscape.difference: PINNs use global neural approximators at collocation points; INN constrains the network to interpolation bases and emphasizes classical convergence behavior.

competitive_landscape.title: DeepONet: Learning nonlinear operators for identifying differential equations based on the universal approximation theorem of operators
competitive_landscape.relationship: Major learned-operator alternative for parametric PDE surrogates.
competitive_landscape.difference: DeepONet learns a function-to-function map through branch and trunk networks; INN directly optimizes mesh-associated interpolation coefficients and tensor factors.

competitive_landscape.title: Fourier Neural Operator for Parametric Partial Differential Equations
competitive_landscape.difference: FNO learns global spectral kernels and resolution-transferable operators, whereas INN uses local interpolation structure and low-rank coefficient grids.

novelty_assessment: The distinctive contribution is the explicit interpolation-valued GNN unification of training, solving, and calibration plus tensor decomposition. The ingredients are related to FEM, generalized bases, PINNs, and tensor compression; broad superiority over contemporary neural operators is not established.
reviewer_notes: Read all 16 extracted pages, including methods and supplementary material references. Competitor records were checked against primary arXiv pages on 2026-08-23; estimated baseline points and evaluation-scope caveats are retained explicitly.
